opening.text: When your phone shows no bars, you cannot call anyone. The phone is fine. The person is there. You just are not connected.
Revelation is a bit like that. God is speaking. The question is whether we are tuned in. Today I want to talk about how God speaks to us and how we can listen.

mainMessage.text: God speaks to His children. He does it through the Holy Ghost, often in a quiet way. We can prepare to hear Him by studying and pondering. We learn to tell His voice from others. And He guides the whole Church through prophets. Revelation is not rare. It is how He leads us home.

blocks.text: God speaks to us.
The Lord told Oliver Cowdery that He would speak in his mind and his heart, by the Holy Ghost. Moroni promised that by the power of the Holy Ghost, we may know the truth of all things.

Yea, behold, I will tell you in your mind and in your heart, by the Holy Ghost, which shall come upon you and which shall dwell in your heart. Now, behold, this is the spirit of revelation; behold, this is the spirit by which Moses brought the children of Israel through the Red Sea on dry ground.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.
President Russell M. Nelson said this in his talk “Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives” from the April 2018 general conference.

I plead with you to increase your spiritual capacity to receive revelation. . . . Choose to do the spiritual work required to enjoy the gift of the Holy Ghost and hear the voice of the Spirit more frequently and more clearly.
The signal is there. We can strengthen our connection.
His voice is often quiet.

We may expect a great sign. But the prophet Elijah learned that God was not in the wind, the earthquake, or the fire. He was in a still small voice. The Lord says that voice whispers through all things.

And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
Yea, thus saith the still small voice, which whispereth through and pierceth all things, and often times it maketh my bones to quake while it maketh manifest, saying:
President Boyd K. Packer of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Personal Revelation: The Gift, the Test, and the Promise” from the October 1994 general conference.

The Holy Ghost speaks with a voice that you feel more than you hear. It is described as a ‘still small voice’ \[D&C 85:6\]. And while we speak of ‘listening’ to the whisperings of the Spirit, most often one describes a spiritual prompting by saying, ‘I had a feeling . . .’
Often we do not hear a voice. We feel a quiet nudge.
We prepare by pondering.
President Joseph F. Smith sat in his room pondering the scriptures. As he pondered, the eyes of his understanding were opened. Pondering invites the Spirit.

On the third of October, in the year nineteen hundred and eighteen, I sat in my room pondering over the scriptures; And reflecting upon the great atoning sacrifice that was made by the Son of God, for the redemption of the world;
As I pondered over these things which are written, the eyes of my understanding were opened, and the Spirit of the Lord rested upon me, and I saw the hosts of the dead, both small and great.
President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency said this in his talk “Serve with the Spirit” from the October 2010 general conference.

Reading, studying, and pondering are not the same. We read words and we may get ideas. We study and we may discover patterns and connections in scripture. But when we ponder, we invite revelation by the Spirit. Pondering, to me, is the thinking and the praying I do after reading and studying in the scriptures carefully.
Pondering takes time. It is worth the time.
The scriptures open the door.

Nephi said angels speak by the power of the Holy Ghost, and the words of Christ will tell us what to do. The Lord told His servants to treasure up His words, and the right words would come when needed.

Angels speak by the power of the Holy Ghost; wherefore, they speak the words of Christ. Wherefore, I said unto you, feast upon the words of Christ; for behold, the words of Christ will tell you all things what ye should do.

Neither take ye thought beforehand what ye shall say; but treasure up in your minds continually the words of life, and it shall be given you in the very hour that portion that shall be meted unto every man.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “Scripture Reading and Revelation” in the January 1995 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

Scripture reading puts us in tune with the Spirit of the Lord. . . . Because we believe that scripture reading can help us receive revelation, we are encouraged to read the scriptures again and again. By this means, we obtain access to what our Heavenly Father would have us know and do in our personal lives today. That is one reason Latter-day Saints believe in daily scripture study.
When we read, we give the Spirit something to bring back to us.
We learn to test what we feel.

Not every strong feeling is from God. Moroni taught that what invites and entices us to do good, and to love and serve God, is inspired of God. The Lord told Oliver Cowdery to trust the Spirit that leads to do good.
But behold, that which is of God inviteth and enticeth to do good continually; wherefore, every thing which inviteth and enticeth to do good, and to love God, and to serve him, is inspired of God.

And now, verily, verily, I say unto thee, put your trust in that Spirit which leadeth to do good— yea, to do justly, to walk humbly, to judge righteously; and this is my Spirit. Verily, verily, I say unto you, I will impart unto you of my Spirit, which shall enlighten your mind, which shall fill your soul with joy;
President Boyd K. Packer of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Personal Revelation: The Gift, the Test, and the Promise” from the October 1994 general conference.

There can be counterfeit revelations, promptings from the devil, temptations! As long as you live, in one way or another the adversary will try to lead you astray. . . . If ever you receive a prompting to do something that makes you feel uneasy, something you know in your mind to be wrong and contrary to the principles of righteousness, do not respond to it!
A true prompt leads toward good. If it does not, we do not follow it.
God also speaks through prophets.
Amos taught that the Lord reveals His secrets to His servants the prophets. The Lord also said that what His servants speak when moved upon by the Holy Ghost is His word and His voice.
Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.

And this is the ensample unto them, that they shall speak as they are moved upon by the Holy Ghost. And whatsoever they shall speak when moved upon by the Holy Ghost shall be scripture, shall be the will of the Lord, shall be the mind of the Lord, shall be the word of the Lord, shall be the voice of the Lord, and the power of God unto salvation.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “If Thou Wilt Enter into Life, Keep the Commandments” from the April 1996 general conference.

Prophets must often warn of the consequences of violating God’s laws. They do not preach that which is popular with the world. . . . Why do prophets proclaim unpopular commandments and call society to repentance for rejecting, modifying, and even ignoring the commandments? The reason is very simple. Upon receiving revelation, prophets have no choice but to proclaim and reaffirm that which God has given them to tell the world.
God guides the whole Church, and He guides each of us.

story.title: Samuel hears the Lord

blocks.text: Samuel was a boy serving in the temple. He heard a voice at night, and he thought it was Eli. Three times he ran to Eli. Then Eli understood.

And the Lord called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child. Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place. And the Lord came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.
Samuel did not know the voice at first. He needed help to recognize it. Many of us are the same. When we learn what it sounds like, we can answer, “Speak, Lord. Thy servant heareth.”

application.text: First, set aside ten quiet minutes each day this week. Read a few verses, ponder, and pray. Second, write down any impression you receive, and act on it if it leads you to do good. Third, say, “Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth,” at the start of your prayer.

story.title: Nephi is led by the Spirit

blocks.text: Nephi went back into Jerusalem at night to get the brass plates. He did not have a plan.

And I was led by the Spirit, not knowing beforehand the things which I should do. Nevertheless I went forth and as I came near unto the house of Laban I beheld a man, and he had fallen to the earth before me, for he was drunken with wine.
He was led one step at a time, not knowing beforehand. He went forward, and the light moved with him. That is how revelation often works. We move, and the next step appears.

application.text: First, pick a question you are facing. Study it out, then ask God about it. Second, take one small step, and watch for the next. Third, write down what you learn, so you remember how He led you.

story.title: Peter knows by revelation

blocks.text: Jesus Christ asked His disciples who they believed He was. Peter answered.

He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God. And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.
Peter did not learn this from a book or a crowd. It came to him from God. Revelation can give us a witness of Jesus Christ that no one else can give us.

But when we ponder, we invite revelation by the Spirit. Pondering, to me, is the thinking and the praying I do after reading and studying in the scriptures carefully.
Pondering holds us steady on the signal.
Fill your mind with good content.
What we put in is what the Spirit can bring back. Nephi said the words of Christ will tell us all things we should do. The Lord said to treasure up His words continually.

Angels speak by the power of the Holy Ghost; wherefore, they speak the words of Christ. Wherefore, I said unto you, feast upon the words of Christ; for behold, the words of Christ will tell you all things what ye should do.

Neither take ye thought beforehand what ye shall say; but treasure up in your minds continually the words of life, and it shall be given you in the very hour that portion that shall be meted unto every man.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “Scripture Reading and Revelation” in the January 1995 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

Scripture reading puts us in tune with the Spirit of the Lord. . . . Because we believe that scripture reading can help us receive revelation, we are encouraged to read the scriptures again and again. By this means, we obtain access to what our Heavenly Father would have us know and do in our personal lives today. That is one reason Latter-day Saints believe in daily scripture study.
Scripture reading keeps us in tune.
Watch out for false stations.
Not every signal is from God. Moroni said that what invites and entices to do good is of God. The Lord told Oliver Cowdery to trust the Spirit that leads to do good and fills the soul with joy.
But behold, that which is of God inviteth and enticeth to do good continually; wherefore, every thing which inviteth and enticeth to do good, and to love God, and to serve him, is inspired of God.

And now, verily, verily, I say unto thee, put your trust in that Spirit which leadeth to do good— yea, to do justly, to walk humbly, to judge righteously; and this is my Spirit. Verily, verily, I say unto you, I will impart unto you of my Spirit, which shall enlighten your mind, which shall fill your soul with joy;
President Boyd K. Packer of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Personal Revelation: The Gift, the Test, and the Promise” from the October 1994 general conference.

There can be counterfeit revelations, promptings from the devil, temptations! As long as you live, in one way or another the adversary will try to lead you astray. . . . If ever you receive a prompting to do something that makes you feel uneasy, something you know in your mind to be wrong and contrary to the principles of righteousness, do not respond to it!
If it leads away from good, change the station.
A wider broadcast.
God also speaks to all of us together. Amos taught that He reveals His secrets to His prophets. The Lord said their words, spoken by the Holy Ghost, are His voice.
Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.

And this is the ensample unto them, that they shall speak as they are moved upon by the Holy Ghost. And whatsoever they shall speak when moved upon by the Holy Ghost shall be scripture, shall be the will of the Lord, shall be the mind of the Lord, shall be the word of the Lord, shall be the voice of the Lord, and the power of God unto salvation.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “If Thou Wilt Enter into Life, Keep the Commandments” from the April 1996 general conference.

Prophets must often warn of the consequences of violating God’s laws. They do not preach that which is popular with the world. . . . Why do prophets proclaim unpopular commandments and call society to repentance for rejecting, modifying, and even ignoring the commandments? The reason is very simple. Upon receiving revelation, prophets have no choice but to proclaim and reaffirm that which God has given them to tell the world.
The prophet speaks to us all at once.

story.title: Ananias is told where to go

blocks.text: Ananias was a disciple in Damascus. The Lord spoke to him in a vision and gave him a strange task.

And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Behold, I am here, Lord. And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and inquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth, And hath seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in, and putting his hand on him, that he might receive his sight.

Ananias had heard that Saul hurt believers. Still, he answered, “Behold, I am here, Lord.” The Lord had been working on both ends. He had spoken to Saul too. Revelation is often like that. God prepares both people before they meet.

application.text: First, tune in each morning with a short prayer. Ask, “What would You have me do today?” Second, read a few verses and ponder them before you start your day. Third, when you get a good prompting, act on it quickly, and write it down.

closingVerse.text: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.

opening.text: When a child is away from home, a good parent wants to hear from them. And a good child answers the phone. A call that goes unanswered does not mean the parent stopped calling.
God is like that parent. He reaches out. Today I would like to talk about revelation, and how we can answer when He calls.

mainMessage.text: God speaks to His children. He uses the Holy Ghost and speaks softly. We get ready to hear by pondering and reading. We learn to tell what is from Him. And He gives the whole Church direction through prophets. When He calls, we can answer.

blocks.text: He is calling.
The Lord told Oliver Cowdery He would speak to his mind and heart by the Holy Ghost. Moroni promised that by the power of the Holy Ghost, we may know the truth of all things.

Yea, behold, I will tell you in your mind and in your heart, by the Holy Ghost, which shall come upon you and which shall dwell in your heart. Now, behold, this is the spirit of revelation; behold, this is the spirit by which Moses brought the children of Israel through the Red Sea on dry ground.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.

I plead with you to increase your spiritual capacity to receive revelation. . . . Choose to do the spiritual work required to enjoy the gift of the Holy Ghost and hear the voice of the Spirit more frequently and more clearly.
He wants to be heard. We can make ourselves ready.
His voice is soft.
Elijah went up to the mountain to meet the Lord. He did not find Him in the wind, the earthquake, or the fire. He found Him in a still small voice. The Lord says it whispers through all things.

And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.
Yea, thus saith the still small voice, which whispereth through and pierceth all things, and often times it maketh my bones to quake while it maketh manifest, saying:

The Holy Ghost speaks with a voice that you feel more than you hear. It is described as a ‘still small voice’ \[D&C 85:6\]. And while we speak of ‘listening’ to the whisperings of the Spirit, most often one describes a spiritual prompting by saying, ‘I had a feeling . . .’
Soft voices are heard by those who are listening.
Sit with the question.
A good conversation takes time. President Joseph F. Smith sat in his room pondering the scriptures. As he pondered, his understanding was opened.

On the third of October, in the year nineteen hundred and eighteen, I sat in my room pondering over the scriptures; And reflecting upon the great atoning sacrifice that was made by the Son of God, for the redemption of the world;
As I pondered over these things which are written, the eyes of my understanding were opened, and the Spirit of the Lord rested upon me, and I saw the hosts of the dead, both small and great.

story.title: Philip follows the Spirit

blocks.text: Philip was told to go down a desert road. He did not know why.

And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship, Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot.

Philip arose and went. He did not wait to understand it first. And on that road, he met a man who was reading scripture and needed someone to explain it. When we answer the call, we often find why it came.

application.text: First, tonight, ask in prayer, “What would You like me to know?” Then be quiet for a few minutes. Second, act on one prompting this week, even a small one. Third, thank God for the times He has already guided you.
